classification.difficultyReason: Compare the complete side-length sets, recognising the common cut and equal 5 cm sides while explaining why the remaining 6 cm and 8 cm sides prevent congruence.

content.prompt: If this triangle is cut as shown, determine whether the two triangles will be congruent. Explain.

spec.description: Unshaded right triangle with vertical 6 cm side, horizontal 8 cm side and two separately labelled 5 cm hypotenuse segments. A red dashed cut joins the lower-left right-angle vertex to the red midpoint on the hypotenuse. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The outer triangle has side lengths 6, 8 and 10 cm. The cut ends at the midpoint of the hypotenuse. No perpendicularity at the cut endpoint is given or drawn.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; the auxiliary variable x is confined to the answer.

answer.short: No. The triangles share the cut and each has a $5\text{ cm}$ side, but their remaining sides are $6\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked: Let the cut have length $x\text{ cm}$. The side lengths are $5, x, 6\text{ cm}$ for one triangle and $5, x, 8\text{ cm}$ for the other. Their sets of side lengths differ because $6\ne8$, so the triangles are not congruent.
